successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: Menabe, 'the southern part of the Sakalava territory'; the modern region of 46,121 km2 is the page's only area

ledger.x: c. 1540: Andriamandazoala founds the Sakalava kingdom of Menabe, by tradition. 'Tradition holds that it was founded by Adriamandazoala (reigned c. 1540 - 1560).' The Sakalava people page puts the first significant kingdoms 'around the 1650s'.
after 1610: Andriandahifotsy 'extended his authority northwards past the Mangoky River' and his sons took the coast 'up to the Tsongay region (now Mahajanga)'.
c. 1690: the Boina kingdom is founded on Boina Bay by Andriamandisoarivo and separates from Menabe.
1820: Radama I begins the Merina campaigns against Menabe.
1822: the last of Radama's three Menabe campaigns.
1834: after the conquest of southern Menabe 'Constant war would ensue' between the Merina and the rest of Menabe until 1846; the page gives no first campaign, so the year is that of the conquest.
1846: 'Constant war would ensue culminating with a Merina victory in 1846.'
August 1897: the Menabe kings fight the French.
1900: the Menabe kingdom ends with its pacification.

wars.name: Merina campaigns against Menabe
wars.outcome: Three ravaging campaigns in 1820, 1821 and 1822; the southern territories conquered in 1834; a Merina victory in 1846 and garrisons in the main Menabe towns; the northern part stayed independent.

wars.name: French conquest of Menabe
wars.outcome: Menabe kings united against the French; the battles of Anosimena and Ambiky (14 and 30 August 1897) killed King Itoera; Menabe 'was not pacified until the year 1900'.

certainty.note: No frontier is described; the Menabe region stands in for the kingdom.
